game.text: Jacksonville at Tennessee, Sunday, October 12, 2014, 1 p.m. ET, LP Field
game.label: Game

attack.text: Make Tennessee defend the same 12-personnel surface several ways. Run Jones-Drew at the actual box count, shift Lewis and Kelce to expose the linebackers' coverage rules, then pair Outside Zone with Boot Flood and Power with Counter and Power Pass. Test whether Woodyard and Brown widen, whether Pollard inserts against the run, and whether Morgan or Wimbley chases the backside. Those are questions to answer on the field, not assumed tendencies.
attack.label: The matchup I am attacking

protect.text: Another game of giveaways and empty trips inside the 30. Pittsburgh got four turnovers and 17 points from them. Protect the ball, give Cousins a defined pressure answer, finish drives, and do not give Locker an open escape lane or Greene an unaccounted cutback. No cheap yards from kick-cover penalties.
protect.label: What I must not give them

change_course.text: If Tennessee packs the run surface, detach a tight end, use Stick or Y-Cross and move the launch point only when the edge is secured. If its linebackers sit on the crossers, work the run and perimeter count. If interior penetration wrecks the mesh point, get to quick throws and protected passes. On defense, if our fits or replacement-pressure exchanges fail, play the clean Under or Nickel Even four-man answer immediately. Medical availability overrides every package.
change_course.label: What would make me change course

contingency.text: Reissue after examination. If Christian Jones is not cleared, Todd Davis takes the eligible linebacker and coverage work. If Brynden Trawick is not cleared, Chris Prosinski practices the deep-safety assignment, Adrian Phillips the supporting safety and kicking roles, and Bouye stays at nickel; recheck the full 46 before naming a new starter. If Jordan Poyer's independent hold remains, he stays inactive. No projected return counts as a clearance.
contingency.label: If Jones, Trawick or Poyer cannot dress

coverage_units.text: Westhoff keeps Hawkins as both returners and Hurns prepared for punt-return relief. Todd Davis, Phillips and Prosinski rehearse the coverage and safety substitutions, with Trawick withheld until medical permission. If Trawick cannot dress, rebuild the seven inactives and the punt, kickoff, dime and emergency-safety groups; do not leave a safety job or kicking lane unmanned. Nicks remains Adams's prepared X relief, not a new starter.
coverage_units.label: Special coverage and substitution consequences

base_personnel.text: Start from 12 and 11, not a fixed run-pass quota. Jones-Drew leads the backs; Anderson relieves him for a prepared series or protection job, with the same credible run-pass menu. Lewis is the established Y and Kelce the movable second tight end and prepared receiving Y. Adams stays at X, Thielen at H, Hawkins at Z; Hurns is general relief and Nicks takes his rehearsed X-relief series. The Monroe-Bitonio-Brewster-Turner-Johnson line stays together. Make Tennessee defend shifts without signaling the ball's destination.
base_personnel.label: Base personnel and roles

learn.text: Who follows the tight ends when 12 shifts toward Empty; how Woodyard, Brown and Pollard fit Power and Outside Zone; whether the backside edge chases Boot; how the front handles a screen release and whether a safety sits on the dig. Bates records the pressure count and Cousins's immediate answer on every shifted look.
learn.label: The first things I want to learn

opening_approach.text: Show the run surface, change the picture with the same people, and return to it once we know the adjustment. Start with secure handoffs and defined reads, then use complementary play-action or the screen only when the defense earns it. A short-yardage, backed-up or scoring situation interrupts this order; an unused idea remains available. No mandatory shot and no target quota.
opening_approach.label: Opening approach

third_down.text: On 1 or 2, Power or the counted Trips run-bubble; on 3 to 5, SCAT Stick or properly protected Mesh; on 6-plus, SOLID Y-Cross, Drive or protected Dagger. Slow Screen is a rush answer, not a surrender throw short of the marker. Cousins identifies the hot defender and the actual line to gain.
third_down.label: Third down

backed_up.text: Inside Zone, Outside Zone, Power and SCAT Stick. No Flea Flicker, long-developing shift or uncovered edge. Win field position without donating the ball.
backed_up.label: Backed up

red_zone.text: High: Y-Cross, controlled run and gated Boot or Power Pass. Low: Counter, Power, Bunch Mesh and Snag by leverage; no forced crosser. Goal line: Power Right or Left and Counter first; a pass only from a taught protection and eligible-receiver count. Review the Week 5 grounding and delay before the snap, not after the series.
red_zone.label: High red zone, low red zone, goal line

two_minute.text: Keep the current 11 group, work Stick, Spacing, Drive, Mesh and Y-Cross through the practiced PRESS procedure. Skalaski gives Cousins the clock and timeouts; get the next call ready on an inbounds completion. A protected shot needs both the field position and clock.
two_minute.label: Two-minute / hurry-up

four_minute.text: Jones-Drew's Power, Counter and Outside Zone are the base; retain Y-Cross or a gated Boot when Tennessee crowds them. First downs end games. Discuss an inbounds completion, sack and opponent timeouts before the series, then use the clock deliberately.
four_minute.label: Four-minute / protect a lead

sudden_change.text: Start with a secure base call unless the safety or rush has already shown the exact shot trigger. Power Pass and Boot come before the Flea Flicker. Never confuse getting the ball after a turnover with permission for a gadget.
sudden_change.label: Sudden change / shot opportunities

front.text: Under against credible tight-end and downhill run surfaces, Nickel Even when the spacing warrants it. Use the established first-unit four-man front. Daryl Smith makes the front declaration; Posluszny and the fit linebacker key Greene's path, the puller and the backside cutback. The force defender keeps outside leverage and the plus-one fitter arrives from the correct side. Do not let a pass look erase the run fit.
front.label: Base front and run fits

coverage.text: Show two-high, play Quarters or Cover 6 by distribution, and use 1 Robber against a real crossing/dig picture. Four rushers with disciplined edges are the default against Locker. We want him to hold the ball to confirm the picture, not escape a vacant lane. Bouye carries Wright's inside release when Wright aligns in his nickel area; Talib and Verner keep their outside jobs. Match Walker's seam and crossing release by rule, not by assigning one linebacker two routes. Replacement rush attacks a verified slide/back scan, never a guessed weakness.
coverage.label: Coverage and rush approach

discover.text: Does Schwenke point the pressure when we mug the interior, and which way does Greene scan? Where does Locker launch and attempt to escape when the edges hold? Who takes Wright when he moves inside, and how does the offense distribute Walker after motion?
discover.label: What we need to discover early

matchups.text: No change. Bouye has the nickel area, Talib and Verner remain outside, Rambo and medically eligible Trawick remain the first safeties, and Prosinski is the sixth defensive back. Daryl Smith owns the front call. Westhoff and Crennel must reconcile any Trawick or Jones absence before dime and the coverage units are approved.
matchups.label: Individual matchups / roles changed

kicking.text: Hawkins returns kicks and punts; Hurns is prepared for punt relief. Scobee, Anger and Kreiter keep the operation. Westhoff checks punt protection, vice, directional placement, lane integrity and the hands unit with the proposed 46. No loose leverage or unnecessary penalty chasing a return. Rebuild each coverage group if Trawick or Jones cannot dress.
kicking.label: Return, coverage and operation instructions

endgame.text: Skalaski gives me actual down, distance, field-goal distance, score, clock, timeouts and challenge status before the choice. Apply the fourth-down rule only after the fourth-down distance and spot are known. Check with the booth before spending a challenge, and leave automatic or final-two-minute reviews to the officials. Cousins and I set the clock goal before two-minute and four-minute possessions. No timeout to rescue an unprepared substitution unless it prevents a worse outcome.
endgame.label: Timeouts, challenges and endgame

participation.text: Reissue after exam. Until the October 7 reassessment and any later clearance, Prosinski takes Trawick's deep-safety teaching work and Phillips rehearses the next safety and coverage duties; Trawick receives only medical-approved work. Todd Davis prepares Jones's linebacker and coverage contingency. Poyer's independent hold remains controlling until released.
participation.label: If a medical assessment changes participation

tradeoff.text: No new Throwback Screen, Halfback Pass, WR Pass or extra motion family this week. Cut optional gadget and peripheral shot repetitions before taking time from ball security, protections, defensive fits or Westhoff's replacement units. Tuesday is off; Wednesday through Friday are helmets, with Saturday walkthrough and no pads in Week 6.
tradeoff.label: What leaves the practice menu to make room

staff.text: Tice owns the offensive installation and next-call information; Bates brings the quarterback's trusted pressure answers; Crennel prepares and transmits my defensive call, with Daryl Smith declaring the front; Westhoff owns kicking operation; Skalaski handles the clock, fourth-down and challenge relay. I call offense and defense. Give me the actual look, the player's assignment, the adjustment and the cost in practice time. Keep correction direct, test it again and let Cousins challenge a call he cannot see. No invented opponent tendency percentages and no play kept only because its drawing looks good.
staff.label: Staff instructions

public.text: We moved the ball against Pittsburgh but gave it away four times and failed to finish too many drives. That starts with me. Tennessee is a division opponent; we need to protect the football, tackle and execute the situations we practice.
public.label: Public position, if I am adding one

open_decisions.text: The final seven inactives and emergency safety/coverage grouping require Jones's October 6 reassessment, Trawick's October 7 reassessment and Poyer's projected October 9 independent-hold release. If any medical result differs, I will reissue the lineup and the affected packages before the game.
open_decisions.label: Other open decisions

ready.text: All three medical decisions are communicated, the final eligible 46 and role replacements are confirmed, the protected shot and pressure checks are reduced, and Westhoff signs off on Saturday's operation and Sunday availability. No game result or completed practice is assumed here.
ready.label: Ready to lock after

calls.condition: Spencer and Yarno verify the release count; do not call against a defender sitting on the back.

calls.reason: Attack a safety who actually drives on Power while maintaining a deep-to-intermediate answer.

calls.reason: Clear the safety with the vertical and work the dig at the sticks.
calls.condition: HALF scan first; convert to the shorter protected answer when a six-man rush threatens the launch point.

calls.condition: Keep the practiced release and escort. If his defender stays, Cousins comes off it.

calls.reason: Compact-space leverage answer when the defense protects the goal line inside.
calls.condition: Stay in its scoring-area role; no illegal rub or blind throw.

calls.reason: A conditional reward only if repeated Power has pulled a safety downhill.
calls.condition: Jones-Drew and Cousins use the retained exchange, MAX protection and covered-shot exit. No trigger or unsettled exchange means no call.

responses.counter: Nickel Even if they spread the run surface and the fitter has a clean check.

responses.reason: Run remains possible; protect the seam and curl while retaining force.
responses.counter: Under if their big personnel are still a credible run threat.

responses.reason: Defend the line to gain and the boot or quick crosser off the run.
responses.counter: No loose edge and no dime against a credible downhill run.

responses.reason: Disrupt inside releases to Wright and Walker while keeping the sticks in view.
responses.counter: If bunch defeats the exchange, simplify to 3 Match.

responses.reason: Keep six defensive backs on the field against an actual pass picture; four rush with contained lanes.
responses.counter: Retain Nickel if substitution or communication is not clean; screen and draw fit stays owned.

responses.reason: Challenge the run surface with a four-man rush, avoid an easy escape outside.
responses.counter: Do not spend a risky fifth rusher just for field position.

responses.reason: Match Walker's seam and Wright's break without surrendering the perimeter fit.
responses.counter: Under if the tight ends attach and run becomes the primary threat.

responses.reason: Compress the windows and keep the immediate flat and quarterback exit covered.
responses.counter: Remove disguise if communication slows near the goal line.

responses.reason: Stop Greene's interior track with force and a designated extra fitter.
responses.counter: Check every eligible tight end before treating it as a pure run.

responses.reason: Protect deep and sideline access while contesting the sticks.
responses.counter: Stay in current personnel if tempo prevents a legal change.

responses.reason: Make Greene earn successive clean fits; tackle inbounds.
responses.counter: Nickel if they throw from spread spacing.

responses.reason: Keep the ball in front and tackle inbounds without gifting free first downs.
responses.counter: If they reach field-goal range in a tight game, contest routes at the sticks.

responses.reason: Give Bouye an inside leverage plan and a declared cross/vertical exchange.
responses.counter: Do not force the nickel job if Wright moves outside; reset the count.

responses.reason: Count all five receivers and challenge the protection without losing the hot lane.
responses.counter: Keep Nickel if tempo prevents dime, and call the simple current-personnel match.

responses.reason: Exchange the field edge for Bouye as fourth rusher and cover the quick answer.
responses.counter: Return to base four if the edge drop, slot exchange or run fit fails.

responses.reason: Change the fourth rusher without losing boundary contain or the hot/curl defender.
responses.counter: Return to base four if Walker or the back becomes unowned.

responses.reason: Use the taught five-man counter only when the immediate throw and coverage behind it are named.
responses.counter: One failed hot coverage or missed contain ends the call.

event.summary: Stone set his Week 6 Game Plan at Tennessee: the call sheet frozen with 21 offensive calls and 17 defensive calls, fourth downs his standing rule, two-point tries his standing rule, kickoffs his standing rule; the 7 inactives Jordan Poyer, Malcolm Butler, Jonathan Grimes, Corey Linsley, Kasim Edebali, Taylor Gabriel, Gator Hoskins; no depth chart change.
